title: Choose a mode in ChatGPT
summary: Find the control beside the message box and try one question at two effort levels.

intro.what: ChatGPT is an app for talking to an AI helper. The model makes an answer. The effort setting tells it how much time to spend working through a problem.
intro.features: Chat can draft text. Search can find a page. Deep research can study several sources. Work can make a document. Codex can edit an app.
intro.exchange: Ask it to explain a pretend mail rule. Try an exception and check it against the rule.
intro.m365: Turn a sample meeting note into a short reminder. Check the day and time.
intro.developer: Describe when your game should end. Ask for a test that proves the ending works.
sources: OpenAI Help · ChatGPT Work and Codex
OpenAI Help · Deep research in ChatGPT

sections.title: Read the menu you have
paragraphs: Open ChatGPT and look beside the message box. On eligible plans, Instant, Medium, High and Extra High use {{model.openai.chat.general}}. Pro uses {{model.openai.chat.pro}} where available. Free and Go have Instant and Think with {{model.openai.chat.free}}. Accounts and features can change. Work and Codex have their own menus, with choices such as {{model.openai.sol.name}} and {{model.openai.astra.name}}.
sources: OpenAI Help · ChatGPT Work and Codex

sections.title: Test an easy rule and a tricky one
paragraphs: Try “Pick the red card from red, blue, gold.” Then try “Keep the red cards, except those with a star.” Give three cards: red star, red dot, blue dot. The second answer should contain only the red dot. If the quick mode misses the exception, try a higher effort. Search for a source when you need a fresh fact.
sources: OpenAI Help · Reasoning settings and availability

title: Pick an OpenAI model for an app
summary: Give each model a test you can mark with an answer key.

intro.what: OpenAI’s API is a way for your app to send a request and get an answer back. The exact model ID tells the service which model to use.
intro.features: The model list names tools for words, pictures and code. A price table tells you the cost of sending in text and getting text back.
intro.exchange: Use pretend mail and ask for one of three labels. Count the labels that match your answer key.
intro.m365: Test whether a helper finds both dates on a made-up project notice.
intro.developer: Try the same broken score button with two models. Run the same test on each fix.

sections.title: Choose one that fits the job
paragraphs: Make a little test with a result you can see. For a picture, pick a screen with a large Help button. For math, use a score you can add by hand. The exact IDs below are for apps.

rows: Build a small feature and test the first version.
Find why a change in one file breaks a button in another.
Read a settings screen and point out the named control.
Read a short list and pull out one field per row.

sections.title: Count the answers you can use
paragraphs: Start with ten short sample notes. Write the right label for each one before you run the test. Check the count, the cost and how long you spent fixing wrong labels. In a paid app, text going in and text coming back can have different prices. Include retries and tool fees when you compare bills.
sources: OpenAI Developers · Model selection and evaluation
OpenAI Help · Codex sign-in and billing choices

exercise.prompt: One run costs $1 and gives eight good answers. Another costs $1 and gives ten. Which costs less per good answer?
answer: The first costs 12.5 cents per good answer. The second costs 10 cents. These are made-up bills to practice the math.

title: Check a source and check a sum
summary: Pick the kind of proof your question needs.

intro.what: Search can look for a web page. Deep research can study several sources. Data analysis can use code to count rows or do math with a file.
intro.features: You can follow source links, review a research plan or check the numbers behind a chart.
intro.exchange: Count two types of pretend mail errors and compare the counts with the sample rows.
intro.m365: Ask for the original rule behind a date in a draft notice. Open the cited page.
intro.developer: Give a score app a table with one blank. Check how it counts completed turns.
sources: OpenAI Help · Deep research in ChatGPT
OpenAI Help · Data analysis with ChatGPT

sections.title: Follow the link to the fact
paragraphs: Use Search for one question, such as when a museum opens on Saturdays. Open the link and look for Saturday on the page. For a bigger job, ask deep research to compare two museums. Ask for opening hours, the date checked and the exact page for each. Read the plan. After the report arrives, pick one row and check it yourself.
sources: OpenAI Help · Deep research in ChatGPT

sections.title: Count the spaces before you draw the chart
paragraphs: One lot has 90 cars in 100 spaces. A second lot has 1 car in 10 spaces. Ask ChatGPT for the share of spaces in use in both lots together. Ask it to show the numbers it added. There are 91 cars and 110 spaces. That gives about 82.7%. The simple average of 90% and 10% treats a small lot as if it had as many spaces as the large one.
sources: OpenAI Help · Data analysis with ChatGPT

title: Choose ChatGPT Work or Codex
summary: Build a Next button and prove that it keeps your place.

intro.what: Work helps make finished items such as a checklist or a slide deck. Codex can make a change in the files that run an app.
intro.features: Codex can work on your computer or in the cloud. It can show the lines it changed and run tests. Work can use the notes and tools you give it.
intro.exchange: Use Work to draft a report from made-up mailbox rows. Use Codex to change the report script.
intro.m365: Turn a short mock agenda into a handout. Check that each decision appears once.
intro.developer: Test a Next button on the first, middle and last pages of a small puzzle book.
sources: OpenAI Help · ChatGPT Work and Codex
OpenAI Help · Using Codex with your ChatGPT plan

sections.title: Pick where the files live
paragraphs: If you want a handout, give Work your sample notes and describe the finished page. If you want a working button, open the app folder in Codex. “Local” means the files on this computer. “Cloud” means another computer reached over the internet. Check that your chosen place contains the latest practice file.
sources: OpenAI Help · ChatGPT Work and Codex

sections.title: Try the button like a reader
paragraphs: Ask Codex for Previous and Next above a puzzle. Tell it to keep a player’s marks. Open the middle puzzle, mark a word and press Next. Press Previous. The mark should still be there. Open the last page and check that Next cannot take you past the end. If the book should work offline, save it first and repeat the test with the network off.
sources: OpenAI Help · Using Codex with your ChatGPT plan

title: Make a picture, try voice and plan a video
summary: Create a nameplate for Coach Alex and check the result at the size it will be used.

intro.what: ChatGPT can make images, edit a picture and talk with you. A transcript is a written copy of spoken words.
intro.features: You can make a still picture, practice a spoken exchange or have the AI draft a shot list. Each job gives you a different kind of result.
intro.exchange: Turn a pretend mail alert into a spoken notice. Check that its code sounds right.
intro.m365: Draft a picture for a practice slide. Keep enough room for the title.
intro.developer: Design a badge for Coach Alex. Check that the name is easy to read on a small screen.

sections.title: Draw the badge for Coach Alex
paragraphs: Open the image tool. Ask for a simple whistle inside a bold circle with space underneath. Keep the words out of the first drawing. Add “Coach Alex” as editable text when you put the badge on a nameplate. Check both words before printing.

ChatGPT’s image tool uses {{model.openai.images.name}}. The API offers {{model.openai.flare.name}} for fast drafts and {{model.openai.sunburst.name}} for fine detail. A cutting machine may need SVG lines. Open the file in your design app and check its size and outlines.
sources: OpenAI Developers · Changes to image models and outputs

sections.title: Ask for speech or for written words
paragraphs: In voice mode, practice asking when a desk opens. Ask for one question at a time and answer aloud. If you already have a sound file, ask for a transcript instead. Check a number by listening to the original. For apps, {{model.openai.voice.name}} is one model for back-and-forth speech. A chat account may show different voice choices.

sections.title: Make a shot list for a movie
paragraphs: The {{model.openai.sora.name}} app and website closed on {{model.openai.sora.app-end}}. Its API closed on {{model.openai.sora.api-end}}. You can still plan a clip in ChatGPT. Ask for three four-second shots of the badge being made. Give that plan to a video tool you can use. Play the final clip and count the shots. Check that the badge keeps its shape.
